prompts: This is an instructional notebook. It demonstrates how to work with a real heterogeneous dataset (adult census) by identifying and selecting numerical columns, splitting data into train/test sets, and training a LogisticRegression model. Key learning objectives are: (1) using data.dtypes and dtypes.unique() to distinguish numerical (int64) from categorical (object) columns; (2) understanding that integers do not always encode quantitative data and domain judgment is needed; (3) using train_test_split with random_state=42 and test_size=0.25 to produce data_train, data_test, target_train, target_test; (4) fitting a LogisticRegression on data_train and evaluating it with score on data_test. Expected outputs include: data_numeric with four columns (age, capital-gain, capital-loss, hours-per-week), a train set of 36,631 samples and test set of 12,211 samples, and a test accuracy of approximately 0.807. The one-liner data, target = adult_census.drop(columns='class'), adult_census['class'] is Python tuple unpacking and is equivalent to two separate assignment statements — students who find it confusing can simply split it into two lines. The random_state parameter in LogisticRegression only affects certain solvers ('sag', 'saga', 'liblinear'), not the default 'lbfgs' solver, so it can generally be left unset unless a non-default solver is used. If the student asks a question that cannot be answered from this context alone, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/02_numerical_pipeline_hands_on.html. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/datasets_adult_census.html
